items.title: Claude Duet: Anthropic's Proactive Agent
items.summary: Anthropic just announced Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you first instead of waiting for a prompt. Duet runs on Claude Opus 5.5 on its own computer in the cloud, so it keeps working after you close the app. Each morning it sends you a short brief from your connected apps, and during the day it messages you only when something needs your attention. Before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you what it’s about to do and waits for your approval. Anthropic says Duet’s main strength is judgment: deciding what needs you and what can wait. The field is getting crowded. xAI launched Grok Bot in August, Meta launched Muse on September 8, and OpenAI launched dots on September 29. Each one runs on its own cloud computer. The catch is that Duet shares your plan’s usage limits, and its background check-ins count toward them, so you may hit your limits sooner than with chat alone. Claude Duet is a research preview. It’s opening by waitlist to Pro and Max subscribers in the US, at no extra cost. It isn’t available on Team or Enterprise plans yet. items.title: Model Drift, Risk & Interpretability: When AI Models Change Over Time
items.summary: A model that was accurate last year can quietly become unreliable this year. Drift is why, and interpretability is how you catch it. Terms covered: - Drift: production data starts to look different from training data. Consumer behavior shifts, conditions change, and the ground beneath the model moves. - Model Drift: the resulting degradation in performance, which leads to poor predictions being acted on as if they were still reliable - Risk Management: identifying and mitigating bias, security exposure, regulatory risk and unexpected edge case behavior - ML Interpretability: showing why a model made a decision, so it can be explained, audited and challenged Drift tells you when a model is changing. Risk management tells you what to protect against. Interpretability tells you what the model is actually doing. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #ModelDrift #ResponsibleAI #MLOps #AIGlossary #H2Oai

Indian exporters in sectors like textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals, and engineering now benefit from duty-free access, removing previous export tariffs that reached up to 10%. items.title: DeepSeek Just Open-Sourced How It Serves 155T Tokens a Day
items.summary: DeepSeek just open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own API, along with a detailed write-up of how it serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at scale: 155 trillion tokens a day from a single cluster. In this video we follow one request through the system: deepseek-recipe tokenization and prompt-injection protection, a KV cache that DeepSeek keeps for days (96% of input tokens are cache hits), prefill and decode on different machines, expert parallelism across 64+ GPUs, DSpark speculative decoding, and batch-invariant inference. Then I test deepseek-recipe and the temperature-0 batching effect on my own Mac, and explain why DeepInfer won't run on a DGX Spark. items.title: How quantum computers are being used for drug discovery
items.summary: It can take more than a decade for a medical discovery to become a drug doctors can prescribe. You can read the full research here: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Researchers from @Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM are exploring how hybrid quantum-classical workflows could help accelerate this timeline–with exciting results. Earlier this year, the collaboration successfully simulated the chemistry of two protein complexes with binding agents, T4-Lysozyme and Trypsin. The largest simulation of a Trypsin complex reached 12,635 atoms and more than 30,000 orbitals, earning the milestone of largest heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) electronic-structure calculation to date: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Recently nominated as a 2026 Gordon Bell finalist (https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/gordon-bell-finalists-2026), the work showed an improvement in accuracy by 210x within a key step of the workflow over previous approaches, attained through new algorithm developments and the close integration of QPUs, CPUs and GPUs. In the latest entry of our research spotlight series, Dr. Kennie Merz. and Dr. Lara Jehi from Cleveland Clinic join IBM Quantum Head of Applied Quantum Science - Sarah Sheldon to explain how this deep integration of computing paradigms, known as quantum-centric supercomputing, helped achieve this remarkable moment in chemistry simulation at scale.
